children: Treasury yields were mixed in European trade Wednesday as investors awaited minutes from the Federal Reserve's October meeting and remarks from several Fed officials, while eurozone bond yields declined.

Investors in the eurozone will focus on second estimate inflation data for October at 1000 GMT, a potential mover of market expectations of European Central Bank rate hikes in December. Money markets price in a 91% probability of a 25-basis-point hike on Dec. 17, according to LSEG.

Money markets currently price in a 98% probability of a 25-basis-point rate increase at the Fed's next policy meeting on Dec. 9, and assign just 2% odds to a 50-basis-point hike, according to LSEG. The minutes of the Fed's October policy meeting, due at 1900 GMT, could shift those expectations.

"The longer the stock market slide endures, the likelier that a 50bp hike in the fed funds rate target will be completely off the table," Thierry Wizman, global FX and rates strategist at Macquarie Group, said in a note.

Financial conditions, after all, have generally tightened since before the U.S. midterm elections earlier this month, as expectations built around Democratic Party gains for federal- and state-level legislatures and executives, he said.

"Notwithstanding the hawkish overtone to market sentiment, the veil of caution created by geopolitical and macro uncertainties is helping to maintain a bid for U.S. Treasurys," Simon Ballard, chief economist at First Abu Dhabi Bank, said in a note.

The two-year Treasury yield rose 0.9 basis point to 4.797%, while the 10-year yield fell 1.2 basis points to 5.090%, according to Tradeweb. The 10-year German Bund yield declined 3.7 basis points to 3.351%.

"We will look for signs of the Federal Open Market Committee being more concerned about inflation than the decision to leave rates unchanged suggested," Kirstine Kundby-Nielsen, senior analyst at Danske Bank, said in a note.
While the likelihood of a larger rate increase in December has essentially been priced out, further tightening is expected.

"Incoming data continues to signal a resilient U.S. economy with elevated inflationary pressures, and the market is pricing in nearly 80 basis points higher policy rates by September of next year--almost 40 basis points more than just two weeks ago," Amanda Sundstrom, senior macro strategist at SEB, said in a note.
While wage inflation continues to moderate, uncertainty over the inflation outlook has increased, putting pressure on the Fed, she said.
Fed Governor Michael Barr, New York Fed President John Williams and Minneapolis Fed President Neel Kashkari are scheduled to speak later Wednesday.
